topic: Sharp full-propensity assignment-information frontier for the ATE. Observe binary Z, finite X and Y in {0,...,K-1}, with overlap and consistency. A compatible full law Q(Y(0),Y(1),Z,X) must match the observed law and satisfy a fixed Gamma bound on the odds distortion of q=P(Z=1|X,Y(0),Y(1)) relative to e(X). Define its Pearson assignment cost R=E[(q-e)^2/{e(1-e)}] and C_P(t) as the minimum R among compatible laws with ATE t. Prove the sharp equivalence t feasible at budget rho iff C_P(t)<=rho, endpoint attainment, the O(|X|K^2)-cell perspective SOCP and explicit conic dual. For binary outcomes, prove a treatment-independent cost-improving garbling to monotone response types, derive the complete six-odds-face scalar catalog plus the unique interior algebraic root, and show the feasible one-stratum null cost equals observed Corr(Z,Y)^2. Prove a one-way cost-nonincreasing embedding of every compatible full law into an explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa-He-Kanamori equation (14), with the exact and locally uniform separation C(0.3)=9/70>9/91=Ctilde_IHK(0.3). Construct simultaneous multinomial profile confidence envelopes with finite-sample O(n^-1/2) diameter on a named uniformly Slater-regular interior region, and prove that honest confidence sets must retain infinite diameter at a contiguous finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary. Uniform tangent inference through zero cells, optimizer ties, and moving odds faces remains an explicit open problem. Consumer: a prespecified categorical-mercury version of Zhang-Zhao's NHANES fish-consumption ATE sensitivity analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A treatment-independent garbling was derived that removes the minority discordant binary response type while preserving observed margins, ATE, odds bounds, and weakly lowering every convex assignment-information cost. It yields six explicit odds faces and one scalar interior root; for the symmetric Gamma=4 witness, C(t)=(0.6-t)^2/(1-|t|) on [0,0.75] and C(0)=0.36. Separate code matched 140 original SOCP solves within 6.2e-10 and 300 garbling checks within 1.2e-16. Exact arithmetic gives C(0.3)=9/70 versus the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of equation (14), valued at 9/91. Boundary checks found infinite null costs, interior active odds faces, and an S5 quintic, so universal radical formulas and globally finite regular vertical bands are excluded. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform stability of the multinomial frontier tangent/profile operator through zero perspective cells and moving odds faces, yielding informative simultaneous confidence sets. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently reconstruct the four-cell garbling, six-face reduction, 9/70 versus 9/91 separation, and asymmetric interior odds-face example; any failure of preservation, monotonicity, or strict separation stops the run. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_avgcase_ate_cost_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the joint full-propensity model with q=P(Z=1|X,Y(0),Y(1)), a fixed Gamma odds cap, and a Pearson assignment-cost budget have an attained sharp ATE cost frontier, rather than only separately sharp bounds for E{Y(1)} and E{Y(0)}?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives sharp second-moment propensity-ratio bounds for each average potential outcome but notes that simultaneous attainment for the ATE may fail or remain unavailable.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: Under the Gamma-only marginal sensitivity model, quantile balancing yields the narrowest compatible ATE interval and establishes sharpness.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn and Kevin Guo
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhang and Zhao optimize treatment-specific propensity ratios and explain that their continuously varying average-case optimizers need not be jointly realizable for the two potential outcomes, whereas Dorn and Guo obtain joint ATE sharpness from the two-point extremal structure of a Gamma-only model. The missing object is a single compatible law for (Y(0),Y(1),Z,X) that simultaneously couples the observed arms while satisfying the pointwise odds restriction and a shared quadratic assignment budget.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-support characterization of C_P(t) as the attained minimum Pearson assignment cost over compatible full laws, together with the exact equivalence that t is feasible at budget rho iff C_P(t)<=rho and attained lower and upper ATE endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest motivation arc for replacing worst-case propensity distortion by average assignment strength and states the relevant ATE sharpness boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Worst-case Gamma is driven by rare extreme confounding -> second-moment propensity distortion measures average confounding -> separate potential-outcome bounds do not settle joint ATE attainability -> a full-propensity ATE frontier is needed.

method_exemplars.technique: Use conditional extremal-weight characterization and an explicit compatible-law construction to prove that optimized armwise bounds are jointly sharp.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the analogous joint-sharpness problem under the Gamma-only odds model; its construction must be replaced where a shared Pearson budget couples strata and response types.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct debiased estimators of sharp sensitivity-bound endpoints with double-sharpness, double-validity, and Wald inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its estimands are sharp ATE bound endpoints under odds-bounded hidden confounding, the same inferential rung required after identifying the Pearson-budget endpoints.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the finite-multinomial Pearson ATE frontier operator uniformly directionally differentiable through zero-probability perspective cells, nonunique optimizers, and changing active Gamma-odds faces, including parameter values where C_P(t)=infinity?

source_refs.claim: Simultaneous multiplier-bootstrap bands are developed under continuous-outcome positive-density and regular influence-function conditions.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: For Gaussian first-stage limits, ordinary-bootstrap consistency requires full differentiability; directionally differentiable maps require derivative-aware resampling.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Marginal optimization is generally not Hadamard differentiable as a value-function map; the paper derives directional derivatives and uniform derivative-bootstrap methods.
source_refs.author: Sergio Firpo, Antonio F. Galvao, and Thomas Parker

open_problems.why_unsolved: Categorical outcomes replace Zhang and Zhao's positive-density quantile geometry by polyhedral and conic active-set changes. Zero empirical cells place the Pearson perspective on its cone boundary, ties can make primal and dual solutions nonunique, and infeasible target values make the profile extended-real. Fang–Santos and Firpo–Galvao–Parker cover directionally differentiable maps with finite regular values, but do not supply uniform tangent calculus for a moving-feasible-set SOCP through support changes and infinity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An extended-real directional derivative and tangent-cone formula for the entire map P_obs -> {C_P(t):t in T}, plus an estimator, joint weak limit, and derivative-aware bootstrap yielding simultaneous confidence sets valid at support and odds-face transitions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its efficient-bound and simultaneous-sensitivity-curve narrative is the regular benchmark that categorical nonregular theory must extend.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average-case bounds form a sensitivity curve -> regular influence functions enable simultaneous bands -> categorical support and active-face changes destroy regular smoothness -> boundary-valid whole-frontier inference is required.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the Hadamard directional derivative and bootstrap the derivative applied to the first-stage Gaussian process instead of bootstrapping the nonsmooth plug-in directly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Active odds faces create the directionally but not fully differentiable structure for which their bootstrap correction was designed.

method_exemplars.technique: Develop uniform weak convergence and resampling for function-valued optimal-value maps using estimated directional derivatives and a bootstrap process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: C_P(t) is an indexed optimal-value function, making their process machinery the closest template for whole-graph bands.

method_exemplars.technique: Use f-divergence generalized empirical likelihood to obtain calibrated confidence regions and expansions for robust optimal values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Pearson assignment cost is chi-square-like, but this smooth-functional machinery must be extended to causal compatibility constraints and nonregular conic faces.

open_problems.open_problem: For finite outcomes and binary treatment, when is the Jensen or conditional-moment relaxation of an f-sensitivity model exactly realizable by a full propensity law, and what is the smallest exact witness of strict inequality for Pearson cost?

source_refs.claim: The paper exhibits conditional-moment feasible weights that are not realizable and leaves open which constraint classes make the relaxed optimum tight with a realizable minimizer.
source_refs.author: Kei Ishikawa and Niao He
source_refs.venue: AISTATS, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 206

source_refs.claim: The expanded convex f-divergence framework identifies coarse uncertainty-set relaxation as a source of conservative policy-value bounds.
source_refs.author: Kei Ishikawa, Niao He, and Takafumi Kanamori

open_problems.why_unsolved: The relaxed program retains observable inverse-weight moments after Jensen projection but drops the cross-world compatibility equations required of one assignment mechanism q(X,Y(0),Y(1)). Ishikawa and He provide a nonrealizable weight example and state that tightness for general f-divergence constraints is open, but they do not characterize equality or quantify the exact numerical loss for a fixed ATE slice.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Necessary and sufficient finite-table conditions for equality between the full-law and Jensen-relaxed values, plus an exact rational binary counterexample reporting both optimal costs and a strict gap.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central narrative is tractability versus sharpness of confounding uncertainty sets, exactly the tension this opportunity resolves.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Full hidden-confounding laws are hard to optimize -> observable conditional-moment and Jensen constraints give convex programs -> relaxation can admit nonrealizable weights -> characterize and measure the exact sharpness loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Dualize conditional f-moment restrictions and compare the full uncertainty set, conditional-moment set, and coarser relaxation by explicit inclusion and nonrealizability constructions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result must reverse or strictly separate the relevant inclusion after restoring cross-world compatibility.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate latent response types and solve the finite compatibility program to certify tight causal bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A binary full-law witness is naturally represented by response-type cells, allowing exact primal certificates rather than only relaxed inverse weights.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate sharp bound endpoints through debiased scores while maintaining validity under nuisance misspecification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the full-law rather than relaxed endpoint is identified, this supplies the nearest sensitivity-analysis template for endpoint inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Can discordant binary potential-outcome types be removed by a treatment-independent stochastic garbling that preserves observed margins, the ATE, and Gamma-odds feasibility while weakly reducing every convex assignment-information cost, and for which convex generators is this reduction valid?

source_refs.claim: Monotone treatment response is imposed as a substantive restriction to learn population response distributions without assumptions on treatment selection.
source_refs.author: Charles F. Manski

source_refs.claim: Sharp binary causal bounds are obtained by representing latent response behavior with finitely many response types and optimizing over their probabilities.
source_refs.author: Alexander Balke and Judea Pearl
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Convex f-divergence constraints provide a language for average assignment distortion, but no response-type garbling reduction is derived.
source_refs.author: Kei Ishikawa, Niao He, and Takafumi Kanamori

open_problems.why_unsolved: Manski treats monotone response as an assumption and Balke–Pearl use response types for sharp linear bounds, while the f-sensitivity literature optimizes distorted weights rather than comparing latent response-type experiments. Searches combining monotone-response garbling with marginal, average-case, chi-square, or Pearson assignment sensitivity found no treatment-independent kernel result. The first new proof step is to construct a Markov kernel on the four binary response types and prove both compatibility preservation and contraction of the perspective-form convex information cost.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A dominance theorem characterizing the convex cost generators for which every feasible binary full law has a monotone-response-type garbling of no greater cost, followed by a complete scalar KKT and odds-face characterization of the reduced optimum.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames assignment-strength sensitivity in the destination literature; the garbling should appear as a structural simplification of that average-case problem, not as an assumption supplied by Manski.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average assignment distortion gives sharper sensitivity analysis -> full-law binary optimization still contains cross-world response types -> a cost-improving garbling may make monotone types without loss -> the reduced odds-face geometry becomes analytically solvable.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode binary potential outcomes as latent response-type masses and certify sharpness using finite-dimensional compatibility constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed garbling acts on the same four-cell response-type representation but adds a convex-information monotonicity argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Express assignment distortion with convex perspective constraints and obtain a strong convex dual.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Perspective convexity is the natural mechanism for proving cost contraction under stochastic garbling and deriving the reduced odds-face dual.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive efficient influence functions for optimized average-case sensitivity bounds and use a multiplier bootstrap for sensitivity curves.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the binary reduction identifies a low-dimensional frontier, this is the nearest inference construction for its estimated endpoints and value function.

open_problems.open_problem: How should a sharp full-propensity Pearson sensitivity frontier for the population ATE be estimated under stratified, clustered, unequal-probability survey sampling when both sampling weights and treatment propensities enter the target law?

source_refs.claim: The paper develops survey-and-propensity-weighted PATE estimators but states that incorporating sampling design into hidden-bias sensitivity analysis remains to be developed.
source_refs.author: Giovanni Nattino, Robert Ashmead, and Bo Lu

source_refs.claim: The marginal-sensitivity bootstrap is illustrated on NHANES fish consumption and blood mercury, but its inferential framework is i.i.d. rather than a stratified multistage survey design.
source_refs.author: Qingyuan Zhao, Dylan S. Small, and Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The average-case analysis revisits the NHANES fish-mercury ATE with cross-fitted one-step estimators and multiplier bands under an i.i.d. sampling model.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Nattino, Ashmead, and Lu separate sample selection from exposure selection and show that the appropriate propensity depends on the available survey weights, but their theory assumes no hidden treatment confounding. The sensitivity papers analyze the canonical NHANES fish-mercury example under an i.i.d. superpopulation approximation. Combining the two is not a mechanical multiplication of weights: full-law compatibility, the Pearson budget, and the ATE must all be defined for the population law, while variance and resampling must respect strata, clusters, and unequal inclusion probabilities.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A survey-design-compatible estimator of the full population frontier and its endpoints, with a joint asymptotic law or replicate-weight bootstrap delivering simultaneous PATE sensitivity bands under stratified multistage sampling.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the fish-consumption and blood-mercury application narrative and explains why sensitivity intervals rather than an unconfounded point estimate are the relevant output.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: NHANES suggests a fish-consumption effect on blood mercury -> unmeasured confounding threatens the IPW estimate -> odds-bounded intervals quantify robustness -> nationally representative claims additionally require survey-design-valid frontier inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine survey inclusion and exposure-propensity weights, then derive variance estimators under a framework distinguishing sample selection from exposure selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the missing complex-survey first-stage law and variance decomposition for the population ATE target.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fitted one-step sensitivity-bound estimators and multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its assignment-strength frontier and NHANES application are closest, but its empirical process must be replaced by a survey-weighted clustered process.

open_problems.open_problem: Can leave-one-covariate calibration of Gamma and Pearson assignment cost be made formally valid and variation-independent for nonlinear finite-categorical propensity models, rather than using empirical maxima or second moments of fitted propensity ratios as approximations?

source_refs.claim: The NHANES analysis describes its worst-case leave-one-covariate calibration as approximate and leaves a more formal Cinelli–Hazlett-style calibration to future work.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: The paper gives formal observed-covariate benchmarking for omitted-variable sensitivity, but its exact factorization relies on regression partial-R-squared geometry.
source_refs.author: Carlos Cinelli and Chad Hazlett
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: A variance-based sensitivity model supplies an R-squared parameter for omitted weighting variables and emphasizes that higher moments affect optimal balancing weights.
source_refs.author: Melody Huang and Samuel D. Pimentel

open_problems.why_unsolved: Partial-R-squared calibration relies on Hilbert-space projection identities for regression residuals, whereas a full-propensity Pearson budget is a nonlinear functional of assignment probabilities and must obey marginalization and cross-world compatibility. Empirical ratios between full and leave-one-covariate propensity fits do not establish that an omitted variable of that strength is compatible with the observed law, nor quantify sampling error when categorical cells are sparse or zero.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp observable benchmarking inequality or equivalence mapping each omitted categorical covariate to an attainable (Gamma,rho) region for the full-propensity model, accompanied by a consistent estimator and simultaneous limit law for the calibrated sensitivity values.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates average-case calibration using observed covariates and explicitly identifies formal calibration as unfinished.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average-case budgets are more interpretable than maxima -> practical use requires comparison with measured covariates -> fitted leave-one-out ratios are only approximate -> a compatibility-aware formal benchmark is needed.

method_exemplars.technique: Factor omitted-variable bias into treatment and outcome partial-R-squared components and benchmark latent strength against observed covariates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the formal benchmarking construction named by Zhang and Zhao, but its projection identities must be replaced by propensity-ratio compatibility geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent nonlinear causal omitted-variable bias through Riesz maps and use debiased machine learning for flexible inference on sensitivity bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It extends formal calibration beyond linear regression and supplies an inferential template for learned nuisance functions, although not for a full-propensity Pearson feasibility frontier.

literature_map:
Tan (2006, JASA) introduced the odds-ratio marginal sensitivity model comparing observed and full-data propensities.
Zhao, Small, and Bhattacharya (2019, JRSSB) reduced empirical IPW sensitivity to linear-fractional programs and used percentile bootstrap, with NHANES fish consumption and blood mercury as the leading application.
Dorn and Guo (2023, JASA) showed those bounds can be asymptotically too wide and obtained sharp Gamma-only ATE bounds through quantile balancing.
Dorn, Guo, and Kallus (2025, JASA) added doubly sharp, doubly valid endpoint estimation and semiparametric efficiency under the odds-bounded model.
Zhang and Zhao (2026, Biometrika; arXiv:2211.04697) replace worst-case-only distortion by a second-moment propensity-ratio budget, derive sharp average-potential-outcome bounds, and construct multiplier-bootstrap sensitivity bands.
The central Zhang–Zhao boundary is that continuously varying armwise optimizers need not be simultaneously attainable for the ATE, unlike the Gamma-only extrema.
Jin, Ren, and Zhou (2026, Operations Research; arXiv:2203.04373) formulate average f-sensitivity through distributionally robust optimization and debiased ERM inference.
Ishikawa and He (2023, AISTATS; arXiv:2302.13348) tighten observable inverse-weight constraints with kernel conditional moments but exhibit nonrealizable relaxed weights and leave the tight-realizability class open.
Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori (2026, JMLR; arXiv:2309.12450) develop a broader convex f-divergence framework; its Jensen and realizability boundary is the closest comparator to a full-law Pearson frontier.
Frauen, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2023, NeurIPS; arXiv:2305.16988) extend sharp generalized sensitivity bounds to richer treatments and effects, but not the joint full-propensity Pearson ATE profile.
Huang and Pimentel (2025, Biometrika) give variance-based weighting sensitivity, while Cinelli and Hazlett (2020, JRSSB) provide observed-covariate calibration in regression geometry; a compatibility-aware Pearson calibration remains absent.
Manski (1997, Econometrica) and Balke–Pearl (1997, JASA) provide monotone-response and finite response-type foundations, but searches found no cost-improving response-type garbling theorem for average assignment-information sensitivity.
Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud) and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics) provide derivative-aware inference for nonsmooth maps; neither covers zero perspective cells or extended-real conic profiles.
Nattino, Ashmead, and Lu (2025, The American Statistician) unify propensity and complex-survey weighting and call for sampling-design-aware hidden-bias sensitivity methods, directly relevant to a nationally representative NHANES analysis.
